images.title: Closest means the smallest gap
images.purpose: Show that closeness to 1 is the size of the gap, so 1.01 is closer than 0.9 even though 0.9 looks near.
images.composition: One horizontal number line with 1 at the centre and four points around it; the smallest gap is the highlighted one.
exact_structure: A horizontal line with a big reddish purple (#CC79A7) dot at 1 labelled 1. Points drawn to scale on the same line, in order: 0.9 left of 1 (gap 0.1), 1.01 just right of 1 (gap 0.01), 1.1 (gap 0.1) and 1.11 (gap 0.11) further right.
Dots for 0.9, 1.1 and 1.11 are amber (#E69F00); the dot for 1.01 is green (#009E73), the closest.
A short green bracket between 1 and 1.01 labelled gap 0.01; a long grey (#6B7280) bracket between 0.9 and 1 labelled gap 0.1.
All five numbers sit on the line in order 0.9, 1, 1.01, 1.1, 1.11, labelled below the dots.
rejection: points not in order 0.9, 1, 1.01, 1.1, 1.11 or not to scale
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The closest number is the one with the smallest gap.
images.description: A number line with the target 1 and the points 0.9, 1.01, 1.1 and 1.11, with the gap from 1 to 1.01 marked as the smallest.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Compare the two brackets and see which gap is shorter.

image_decisions.why: Comparing gaps, not first digits, decides which decimal is closest.
